dedupe_keys.name: usgs estimates of subsurface tile drainage extent 12 midwest states 2012 conterminous us early 1990s

description: These two U.S. Geological Survey data releases are 30 m rasters of the estimated extent of subsurface tile drainage on farmland. The ScienceBase pages say the 2012 layer for 12 Midwest states (South Dakota, Nebraska, Kansas, Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri, Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky) allocates state-level "land drained by tiles" acreage from the 2012 Census of Agriculture to cultivated cropland from NLCD 2011 on poorly drained soils, and that the national layer for the early 1990s does the same from county-level drained acreage (Sugg, 2007) with STATSGO soils, excluding federal land. Both were published on 25 April 2016 by Naomi Nakagaki, Michael Wieczorek and Sharon Qi as GeoTIFFs of about 167 MB and 884 MB with preview images and metadata, downloadable and free (USGS data; the licence is not stated on the pages read). Caveats: tile locations are allocated by rule, not mapped, so they show where drainage is likely, not actual drains. For simulation they locate agricultural drainage networks that speed nutrient and flood flows to rivers, useful for flood, water quality and drainage infrastructure models in farm catchments. Related catalogue records include the ACPF database.
